name: ping
description: Sends ICMP echo requests to test reachability and measure round-trip time.

commands.explanation: Sends echo requests until Ctrl-C and reports latency and loss.
Stops after n packets — what you want in scripts.
Changes the interval; below 0.2 s needs root.
Waits at most n seconds for a reply.
Sets payload size. With -M do (do not fragment) this finds the path MTU: 1472 + 28 bytes of headers = 1500.
Prints a timestamp before each line.
Reads the TTL in the reply to guess the OS: about 64 for Linux and macOS, 128 for Windows, 255 for network gear.
Pings a broadcast address; most modern hosts ignore it.

commands.command: for i in $(seq 1 254); do ping -c1 -W1 <prefix>.$i | grep "bytes from" & done; wait
commands.example: for i in $(seq 1 254); do ping -c1 -W1 192.168.1.$i | grep "bytes from" & done; wait
commands.explanation: A quick ping sweep with nothing but bash — useful on a foothold without nmap.
